summary: Unexpected duplicate external tool invocations when retrying streaming responses using Python async SDK
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their async Python client sends a streaming generation request that triggers an external tool/function call (via function-calling), a client-side retry (triggered by a client timeout/error) results in the external tool being invoked twice.

Impact: Duplicate downstream side-effects (webhook notifications and payment capture) at a paying enterprise customer. Reproducible in production for NarrativeHealth, ~3x/day, causing billing and safety concerns.

Environment: Redwood dedicated prod cluster (us-east), customer using SDK v0.9.12 (python), streaming=True, function_call enabled, custom tool adapter that executes an HTTP POST to customer finance endpoint.

Expected behavior: Retry should be idempotent for function/tool calls if caller provides idempotency key or if the SDK handles function-calling idempotency for streaming flows. The second attempt should not trigger duplicate external side-effects.

Actual behavior: When the initial streaming response fails mid-stream (client-side read timeout or connection reset) and the client retries the call, the platform executes the function/tool callback again. The SDK retry path currently re-sends the request without a stable idempotency token for the function call portion, resulting in duplicate external requests.

Steps to reproduce (minimal):
1) Use python async SDK v0.9.12 with streaming=True and an async wrapper that retries on TimeoutError after 2s.
2) Provide a function schema for a single endpoint that triggers an outbound POST (customer tool).
3) Start generation and simulate network flakiness by killing the streaming connection mid-response (e.g., drop TCP or raise asyncio.TimeoutError in client).
4) Client retry kicks in and re-sends request. Observe two POSTs received by the external tool.

Relevant logs and snippets (customer-provided):
```# simplified pseudo-code
async def call_model_with_retry(prompt):
    try:
        async for chunk in client.generate_stream(prompt, streaming=True, functions=[...]):
            process(chunk)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        # client retry
        await client.generate(prompt, streaming=False, functions=[...])
```
Received webhook POSTs at: 2026-03-11T15:04:12Z and 2026-03-11T15:04:15Z for the same prompt_id.

Customer has temporarily disabled streaming and uses non-streaming calls as a mitigation. They are requesting a permanent fix or recommended guidance for safe retries with streaming and function-calling.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Opened internal ticket INT-512 to coordinate with SDK and Serving teams. Asked customer for request_id, full request headers, and sample tool webhook payloads.

2026-03-12 - Customer (NarrativeHealth - infra@nh.example): Provided request_id=nh-prod-7f3b, sample payloads, and noted SDK usage pattern above. Confirmed duplicate POSTs are causing payment gateway reconciliations to fail.

2026-03-13 - Diego Rivera (Engineer): Initial hypothesis: idempotency token for function-calling is created after stream completion acknowledgement, so mid-stream failures leave the call unregistered; retry path generates a new token. Reproduced locally with SDK v0.9.12 using a mock tool that logs POSTs.

2026-03-13 - Diego Rivera (Engineer): Added logs from serving-runtime showing two separate function_call_start events with different call_id values for the same client request hash when the client retried. Linking serving trace: https://trace.redwood.internal/trace/abc123 (internal only).

2026-03-14 - Support: Shared workaround while we investigate: (1) Disable streaming for requests that trigger external side-effects; (2) Use SDK-provided idempotency_key parameter on function calls (if available) to ensure dedup on the tool side; (3) Set client-side retry to only retry non-committing operations. Customer applied (1) and saw duplicates stop.

2026-03-14 - Engineering (Diego): Drafted internal plan: (A) Short-term: add SDK helper ensure_function_call_idempotency() that injects a stable x-redwood-func-id header before the request is sent, including for streaming flows; (B) Long-term: modify runtime to register pending function calls earlier in the request lifecycle so retries can be reconciled. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/418 .
investigation_notes: Reproduction: Local reproducer built by engineering. Failure mode reproduces when stream is interrupted between model token emission and function_call completion acknowledgement.

Root cause hypothesis: Race between streaming lifecycle and function-call idempotency registration. SDK currently waits for function_call completion to attach stable idempotency metadata to the request context; if the client aborts mid-stream, there is no recorded idempotency token and a retry generates a fresh call_id.
Serving logs: Observed two function_call_start events with different call_id for same client request hash. No server-side dedup key present in the earlier attempt.

SDK codepath: async streaming path splits generation and function-calling flow; retry wrapper re-enters top-level generate call and does not reuse previous function-call metadata unless the caller provided an idempotency_key.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: disable streaming for endpoint that triggers external side-effects OR provide an explicit idempotency_key in the request's function call metadata. Customer accepted workaround and reverted to non-streaming for now.

Short-term fix: SDK patch to v0.9.13 will expose helper argument function_idempotency_key and will set a stable header (x-redwood-func-id) for streaming requests before the first chunk is sent. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/418 (under review).
Long-term action: runtime change to register pending function calls earlier so that retries can be reconciled independent of streaming completion. Tracked in INT-512.

Follow-ups: QA test covering streaming interruption + retry + function-calling added to pre-release test matrix. Notify NarrativeHealth when v0.9.13 is released; schedule a post-deploy verification window with customer for 48 hours.
